gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Edo SZ draws its lowercase with a plotter-pen line, standing like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified without growing, with terminals stopping well short of the stem, so paragraphs read with generous ease.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement reads stocky, its round forms curving like open parentheses and its middle band filling the line. A full page feels dense and sturdy, with Edo SZ's uniform curves above.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Edo SZ bends each letter like a paperclip, with no swelling or thinning, and a lowercase built like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Tangsa's inviting round letters keep that wire-like heading approachable.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC lets its curves flare outward rather than curl inward. Edo SZ is best at bold, tubing-like loops of one constant stroke, while the body is best at generous counters that keep text clear.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Clean and spacious, Noto Sans Thai Looped has deep-bodied lowercase that looks bold, with generous gaps where its curves end. Edo SZ's unmodulated strokes lead like a rail, with the body filling below.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Approachable and clean, Noto Sans Ugaritic leaves its letter mouths open like unjoined chalk arcs, with capitals barely above the lowercase. Give Edo SZ's unit-width stroke plenty of size to show off.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Edo SZ lays down a plain stripe of constant ink, and its lowercase carries itself like iron capitals. Noto Sans Vithkuqi, with open throats and a minimal step up to capitals, gives it a modern, clean partner.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-numans: Numans reads loose and rope-thick, its s ends hanging far from the spine and its tracking pushed well beyond normal. Edo SZ keeps diagonals firm, while Numans does the spreading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-onest: Edo SZ stamps a single constant stroke across its iron-like lowercase. Onest settles into paragraphs easily, with short ascenders over big bowls and a gentle line that never pools ink at the turns.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-oxygen: Plain wire, iron-sized: Edo SZ holds one constant line width and a lowercase with cast iron capital presence. Oxygen supports it with curves that never close back on themselves and lowercase close to its capitals.
